headlines.story:
Golden State Warriors center Charles Bassey says his continued presence in the NBA, after repeated injury setbacks, is a reflection of the adversity he has had to overcome.

The Nigeria-born center is in his sixth NBA season after earning a return to Golden State with a productive finish to the previous campaign. But another knee problem delayed his start this season, extending an injury history that has twice ended his seasons prematurely with San Antonio Spurs.

"Obviously, I've had injuries and I'm still here, so it's been a long, adverse journey," Bassey said in a video posted by the Warriors on social media.

The center missed Golden State's first two games with knee tendinitis before scoring 10 points and collecting seven rebounds, with two blocks, in a 131-122 loss at Phoenix on Oct. 24. He made all four of his field-goal attempts in just under 13 minutes.

That performance followed the five-game stretch that helped secure his return to the Warriors. Signed late last season, Bassey averaged 10.6 points and 7.2 rebounds before agreeing to a one-year deal in July.

His opportunity in Golden State came after a season spent moving between NBA teams and the G League. He had appeared for Memphis, Philadelphia and Boston before the Warriors picked him up in April.

On his 26th birthday, the Warriors star looked back to his basketball beginnings and said even the decision to take up the sport required some persuasion.

"It's been a long journey. Obviously, I grew up playing soccer in Nigeria," he said. "I was trying to sell chicken to this dude, but I didn't know he was a coach. He coached basketball, so he talked to me.

"I wasn't interested because I still loved playing football. It took me a minute to just give it a try but I finally did and I liked it."

That decision eventually took him to the United States and Western Kentucky.

"I came to the States, and I went to college, got drafted into the league," Bassey said.

Philadelphia selected him with the 53rd pick in the 2021 NBA draft. By then, he had already recovered from a tibial plateau fracture in his left leg that ended his sophomore college season in December 2019.

The injuries followed him into the NBA.

After joining San Antonio in 2022, Bassey averaged 5.7 points and 5.5 rebounds in 35 games before a patella fracture ended his season in March 2023. That December, he tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee while playing for the Austin Spurs in the G League, ending another season.

He returned to make 36 appearances for San Antonio in 2024-25, but his next sustained opportunity came in the G League. Santa Cruz acquired him from Delaware in December 2025, bringing him into the Warriors' organization.

Across 20 G League regular-season games with Delaware and Santa Cruz last season, he averaged 20.5 points and 12.5 rebounds, becoming the only qualifying player to average at least 20 points and 12 rebounds. It was enough to convince Golden State to sign him after that run.

But his minutes remain limited early this season. After the Phoenix performance, he went scoreless with one rebound in Golden State's 134-114 victory at Denver on Oct. 26.

That Phoenix offered an early opportunity to build on his brief run with Golden State last season, although his limited minutes in Denver showed he is still working to establish a regular role.

headlines.story:
MINNEAPOLIS -- Golden State Warriors superstar Stephen Curry eclipsed 40 points for an NBA record 46th time since his 30th birthday, needing his best statistical night of the early season to beat the Minnesota Timberwolves 119-114 on Wednesday night.

Curry's 44-point night was a performance fueled by the game plan. The Warriors' coaching staff wanted to get Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert out of the paint, so they spammed high-screen action with Curry in the first half to drag Gobert into space.

It worked. The reeling Timberwolves, playing their first game since losing Anthony Edwards to an arthroscopic procedure on his right knee, were scattered in their coverage on the back end and an aggressive Curry shredded them.

Two nights earlier, the Denver Nuggets sold out to stop Curry, and he attempted only one shot in the first half, finishing an efficient but tame 8-of-8 from the field.

On Wednesday night, Curry fired up six shots in the first seven minutes and then 10 more in the second quarter. At halftime, he had 23 points on 8-of-16 shooting, including five 3s. The fifth came from 31 feet out, an audacious attempt that always signals an in-rhythm Curry.

"I'm just watching like, man, this guy is good as hell," Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg said. "It's crazy. I caught myself shaking my head a couple times."

The Warriors led by as many as 24 points, but Minnesota eventually forced a batch of turnovers, sped up the older team and threatened deep into the fourth quarter.

Despite wobbly moments, Curry and the Warriors ultimately closed. He dove on the floor for a third-quarter loose ball, telling reporters later it was a sign of how well his body was feeling on a night he eclipsed 30 minutes for the first time this season.

In the fourth quarter, despite cooling off from the field, Curry buried the Timberwolves at the free throw line. He made all seven of his free throws in the final eight minutes and finished 16-of-16 from the line.

"We still have a lot of things to [improve], but you like learning lessons while you're winning," Curry said. "The 2-1 road trip is great. Step in the right direction."

The Warriors opened the season with three straight losses, including a 12-point collapse in the final three minutes of their home opener against the Memphis Grizzlies. Considering the daunting schedule ahead, there was a slight bit of panic about an early-season spiral.

But the Warriors have since responded. They blew out the Nuggets in Denver on Monday night behind 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists from Lendeborg in his fourth career game and then survived against the Timberwolves behind a fresh Curry.

"There's a slight bit of relief," Curry said. "But still an understanding that in the Memphis game, the second half tonight, we know we can play better."

Lendeborg finished with 26 points and nine rebounds against the Timberwolves, but Warriors coach Steve Kerr said the rookie was in a sour mood postgame because of his seven turnovers.

"I played hella soft today," Lendeborg said.

The Warriors return to San Francisco for a six-game homestand that begins with Luka Doncic and the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night. The Lakers crushed the Warriors in the opener and Lendeborg got in a memorable dustup with Doncic that spilled over into the postgame news conferences.

Asked whether he was looking forward to the rematch, Lendeborg said, "Absolutely."

"Yes, I am," he said. "I'll talk about that more on Friday."

headlines.story: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Quentin Grimes scored 23 points, Collin Sexton added a season-high 21 points off the bench, and the Los Angeles Lakers — without Luka Doncic — beat the Los Angeles Clippers 103-87 on Wednesday night for the second time in a week. Doncic sat out with back tightness from the second game of the team’s first back-to-back of the season. Starting forward Ziaire Williams missed the game with a sore left foot. Coach JJ Redick said both moves were precautionary. Without Doncic's NBA-leading 36-point average, the Lakers (4-1) had six players in double figures. Austin Reaves had 16 points and Matisse Thybulle had 15. Sexton and Thybulle had four 3-pointers each. Rookie Keaton Wagler scored a career-high 21 points off the bench to lead the Clippers (1-3). They dropped their third in a row, having lost to the Lakers by eight points on Friday. They were without starting forward Rui Hachimura (left quad tightness) against his former team. The Clippers again failed to hold onto the ball with 24 turnovers. They had 26 in each of their last two games, both losses to the Thunder and Lakers. Down 18 points, the Clippers briefly rallied to open the third, outscoring the Lakers 12-2 to pull within seven. But the Lakers closed the quarter on a 27-15 spurt, with Sexton reeling off 11 consecutive points including back-to-back 3-pointers for an 85-65 lead. The Lakers took control in the second quarter, outscoring the Clippers 31-6, including 16 points in a row, to take a 56-38 halftime lead. Six different players scored for the Lakers, led by Reaves with nine. Up next Lakers: At Golden State on Friday night to open NBA Cup group play. Clippers: At Minnesota on Friday night to open NBA Cup group play. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headlines.story: DALLAS -- — Cooper Flagg had 26 points and eight assists and P.J. Washington scored 18 points as the Dallas Mavericks beat the injury-depleted Oklahoma City Thunder 120-96 on Wednesday night. The Mavericks (3-2) led by 12 in the first half and by 27 in the fourth quarter to move over .500 for the first time since Flagg joined the team last fall. Dallas' Kyrie Irving scored 15 points, 13 in the first half when he hit his first four shots, including three behind the arc. It was Irving's first home regular-season game since March 3, 2025, when he suffered a torn ACL in his left knee. Irving sat out Dallas’ home opener last week on the second half of a back-to-back. Ajay Mitchell scored 29 points and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 21 for the Thunder (4-1). Oklahoma City played its second game of the extended absences of Jalen Williams (broken leg, dislocated ankle) and Cason Wallace (torn labrum) and also the second without Chet Holmgren (patellar tendinitis in his right knee). Alex Caruso also sat out with patellar tendinitis that sidelined him during Monday’s home win over Phoenix. It was the first home victory for first-year Mavericks coach Dusty May on his second try. The Mavericks dominated from downtown. They sank a season-best 16 3-pointers on 45 attempts, with 11 made in the first half. The Thunder were a season-low 5 of 32 behind the arc for a season-worst 15.6%. Those were also lows for a Mavericks opponent this season. Dallas’ accuracy from distance included center Daniel Gafford’s first 3 in eight NBA seasons on his 2,384th career shot. Gafford missed one 3-point try previously, on March 29, 2022 with Washington. Up next Both teams will face the Houston Rockets next, Dallas at home on Friday and Oklahoma City on the road on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headlines.story: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Victor Wembanyama had 36 points and 14 rebounds, and the San Antonia Spurs beat the short-handed Utah Jazz 117-111 in overtime on Wednesday night. Devin Vassell scored 17 of his 21 points after halftime to give the Spurs (3-2) a second option that was missing early on as Utah (1-4) led by as many as 11. Keyonte George had a season-high 31 points but seemed gassed at the end of regulation and overtime carrying the Jazz offense. Ace Bailey added 19 points and rookie Darryn Peterson had 18 but didn't play down the stretch or in overtime. Brice Sensabaugh, who scored 16 points, opened overtime with a 3-pointer for the Jazz but the Spurs responded with a 12-0 run to secure their third straight win. San Antonio's aggressive defense disrupted every Jazz offensive action and forced desperate shots near the end of the shot clock in the extra period. The Spurs caused four turnovers and allowed just 2-for-7 shooting in overtime. With the Jazz trailing 105-100, Sensabaugh and George hit back-to-back buckets to send the game into overtime. The Spurs missed their last four field goal attempts in regulation, including De’Aaron Fox's jumper at the buzzer. The Jazz were playing without three of their big men starters. Jaren Jackson has a torn MCL in his right knee, Lauri Markkanen has a right wrist sprain and Jusuf Nurkic has yet to play this season with a foot injury. San Antonio's Tobias Harris hasn't played this season because of a strained calf but the Spurs have one of the best health outlooks of any Western Conference contender. Wembanyama scored 21 in the first half to keep the Spurs within striking distance but they trailed 55-51 at the break. Up next Spurs: Host Minnesota on Saturday. Jazz: Host Portland on Saturday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

headlines.headline: Nikola Jokic records 200th career triple-double in Nuggets' win over Pelicans
headlines.description: Denver's Nikola Jokic had 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists for his 200th career triple-double Wednesday night as the Nuggets beat the Pelicans. He needs 10 more to supplant the retired Russell Westbrook as the NBA leader.
headlines.title: Nuggets' Nikola Jokic records 200th career triple-double
headlines.linkText: Jokic notches 200th career triple-double, now 10 behind Westbrook for NBA lead
headlines.story:
NEW ORLEANS -- Nikola Jokic had 21 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists for his 200th career triple-double in the regular season, and the Denver Nuggets never trailed in a 104-91 victory over the winless New Orleans Pelicans on Wednesday night.

Jamal Murray scored 23 points, and Aaron Gordon added 15 points and 11 rebounds for the Nuggets, who swept a two-game, home-and-home series with New Orleans.

After overcoming a 23-point deficit to beat the Pelicans in Denver on Saturday, the Nuggets this time raced to a 22-point lead in the first half and maintained a comfortable margin most of the way.

Zion Williamson scored 25 points for the Pelicans, hitting a fourth-quarter 3 that pulled New Orleans as close as 88-83. Murray responded with a 3 and a driving finger roll to push the Nuggets' lead back to 10.

Jokic needs 10 more regular season triple-doubles to supplant Russell Westbrook, who retired after last season, as the NBA leader. Westbrook reached 200 triple-doubles in his 1,175th game; Jokic did it in his 814th. They are the only two players in NBA history to eclipse 200. 

Sixteen of Jokic's triple-doubles have come against the Pelicans, six more than any other opponent. 

Christian Braun scored 15 points and Trevon Brazile added 11 points for Denver, which entered the game with several injuries and used just nine players.

Derik Queen had 11 points and 12 rebounds, and Jeremiah Fears scored 11 points for the Pelicans, who are 0-4 under first-year coach Jamahl Mosley

Murray made his first three shots -- all from deep -- and Denver shot 62% in the first quarter while building a 37-18 lead. Marvin Bagley's runner gave Denver its largest lead at 44-22 with about nine minutes remaining in second quarter.

The Pelicans struggled from the perimeter, hitting just 7 of 30 3-point attempts (23.3%).

Denver played without Cam Johnson (ankle) and Alpha Diallo (sprained wrist) and continued to be without Julian Strawther and Spencer Jones.

ESPN Research and The Associated Press contributed to this report.

headlines.story: MINNEAPOLIS -- — Stephen Curry scored a season-high 44 points, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg had 26 and Golden State Warriors held on Wednesday night for a 119-114 victory over the Minnesota Timberwolves, who were without injured guard Anthony Edwards. The Warriors have won two straight after opening 0-3, while Minnesota has dropped two in a row after starting 3-0. Wednesday was the first test for Minnesota to see how its lineup would look without Edwards. The Timberwolves announced Tuesday that Edwards would miss extended time after arthroscopic surgery on his right knee. Edwards averaged 33.3 points through Minnesota's first four games. Curry shot 11 of 27, including six 3-pointers, and was 16 of 16 on free throws. He also had eight rebounds and six assists. After trailing by 24, the Timberwolves climbed back in the fourth quarter thanks to Jaden McDaniels and Jonathan Kuminga. Trailing 116-112, Minnesota had multiple chances to make it a one-possession game but McDaniels missed two shots from deep in the final minute. Kuminga led Minnesota with 20 points against his former team. Kuminga was drafted seventh overall by Golden State in 2021 and was traded to Atlanta midway through last season. He signed as a free agent with Minnesota in September. McDaniels and Terrence Shannon Jr. each had 19 points. Wolves guard Lamelo Ball struggled from the floor for the second straight game. He finished 3 of 11 from the field and 2 of 8 from 3-point range to finish with just eight points. Up next Warriors: Host the Los Angeles Lakers on Friday night. Timberwolves: Hosts the Los Angeles Clippers on Friday night. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here
